The function $q(x)$ is defined and differentiable on $[1,9].$ The graph of ${q}^{′}(x),$ the derivative of $q(x),$ is shown above, where the area of the region between the graph and the $x$-axis is $12.$

Given that $q(9)=-1,$ what is the minimum value ${q}_{\text{min}}$ of $q(x)$ on the interval $[1,9]?$

${q}_{\text{min}}=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
According to the candidates test, the minimum value of $q(x)$ on $[1,9]$ must occur at a critical point or an endpoint of the interval.

**Step 1**: Find the critical points:

We see that ${q}^{′}(x)$ is defined everywhere on $x\in (1,9),$ and ${q}^{′}(x)\ne 0$ inside the interval. Therefore, the candidates are $x=1,9.$

**Step 2**: Compute the value of $q$ for each candidate using the fundamental theorem of calculus:

Using the given information and the fundamental theorem of calculus, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}q(9) & =-1 \\ q(1) & =q(9)+{\int }_{9}^{1}{q}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =q(9)-{\int }_{1}^{9}{q}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-1-12 \\  & =-13\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Select the smallest value of $q$ from our candidates.

Comparing the values of $q$ found in step $2,$ we have

$$
{q}_{\text{min}}=min\{-1,-13\}=-13.
$$

Therefore, the minimum value of $q$ is ${q}_{\text{min}}=-13,$ and the value of $x$ that minimizes $q(x)$ is ${x}_{\text{min}}=1.$
